title: Rumor / Omen / Clue (d100)
note: A rumor, omen, superstition, or clue — from the AP Idle Rumors table, the Eight Practices, and Willowshore gossip. (T)=true, (F)=false, (?)=unverified town-talk; the player hears the rumor, not the tag — keep truth GM-side and let play sort it out. Gather Information in town = a few hours + DC 15 Diplomacy (better at the Happy Kappa). Many entries foreshadow NPCs and threads; none reveal a GM-ONLY secret outright. Use freely to seed scenes, give grateful locals something to share, or add seed-deck novelty.

entries.value: Old Matsu had six different lady visitors last spring — folk say he's hunting a wife in his old age. (F: he's just lonely.)
They say herbalist You So-Jin used a ghost to make her First Long Night lantern glow. (F: an old slander; she's a healer, not a necromancer.)
That feral cat, Yami, that haunts the old Cerulean Teahouse — there's more to it than a cat. (T.)
The giant stag beetle's territory is creeping toward town — is somebody feeding it? (F: it's just the season.)
There were winter sightings of the Fox Ghost out in the woods. (F, say the skeptics — but they say it quietly.)
See a crane, leave it be: good luck to see one, terrible luck to kill one. (T.)
The old monastery at the far end of the Pilgrim's Path is truly haunted — that's why no one ever goes. (T.)
The Great Willow up the Trimountains gives gifts to those who please it. (T.)
An outrageous, almost-certainly-untrue rumor about one of the PCs is making the rounds. (F — improvise it.)
Practice 1: whatever you do, don't call a ghost a ghost — naming it invites it in. (Hotly debated whether it works.)
Practice 2: never pat someone on the head or shoulders this season — you might pat something wearing their shape.
Practice 3: don't go into the water when a ghost is near — that's how they pull you under.
Practice 4: don't eat food with two stick-like things poking out of it; that's an offering to the dead, not a meal.
Practice 5: don't lean against walls in daylight — the cold that leans back isn't the wall.
Practice 6: never whistle at night, or something will whistle back and follow the sound home.
Practice 7: bring the laundry in before dark — what wears it overnight gives it back.
Practice 8: if a voice calls your name from behind you at night, do NOT turn around.
Keep the town lanterns burning — an unlit lantern signals an abandoned town and invites ghosts, vermin, and worse inside. (T, by old Shenmen custom.)
The Eternal Lantern on Dawnstep Bridge was Master Zhi Hui's own gift, and so long as it burns the town is safe. (T.)
Ugly Cute, the stone spider at the Spider Gate, has a guardian spirit living in it that watches over the town. (?: villagers swear by it.)
The Matsuki Estate walls are mixed with blessed salt and holy water — that's why the monsters never breached them. (T.)
Blacksmith Yong Wu-Xiu can work cold iron and silver — but only for folk she counts as friends. (T.)
The Pharasmin priestess Elizeth plays her flute alone in the graveyard at night to keep the recently buried calm. (T.)
Fifteen years back a skulk of foxes drove off the imperial guards to save a hidden baby at the Nine Ear Shrine — that baby grew up to be the priest there. (T.)
Woodraft Lake drowned Lady Nanbyo's old shrine; the governor who pushed the dam was buried by a landslide on a clear sunny day. Folk treat the lake as her shrine now. (T.)
Don't bury your dead in the ground — cremate them, the way the old settlers did, or they don't always stay down. (?: an old Southbank custom.)
Someone's been hanging posts strung with paper shuriken out at the Bones of the Forgotten — like they're afraid one of the buried criminals will rise angry. (T: someone fears a vengeful ghost.)
The empty lot downtown where the governor's manor, bank, and treasury stood — nobody can quite say what became of Governor Heh or his estate. (T: a real and troubling mystery.)
The Industrial District bosses fled with the empire, but the governor still made the workers keep at it — Kawaka holds secret meetings to free those who want out. (T.)
Granny Hu, the retired guard captain, is the real power in this town — more than the watch, more than the governor. (T: more than most guess.)
Packages move through the Trade Office that aren't in any ledger, headed out to the Mushroom House. (?: dangerous to ask about.)
Exchange Manager Kim Gu-won hates his post and took it like a man with no choice. (T — and there's a reason he can't quit.)
The late aristocrat Qing Mai-Lai died last winter with no will, so nobody owns the Cerulean Teahouse — it's just sitting there. (T.)
There's an abandoned shrine to Desna behind the old lumber-lord estates; folk feel someone ought to take the goddess in before she's wholly forgotten. (T.)
Master Zhi Hui found the sacred sugi grove by following the Great Willow's guidance, and built the monastery around it. (T: town legend.)
Long ago a hero slew a great evil on the Trimountain and a sugi tree grew over the grave to keep it down — the town's founding legend. (T, told as folktale.)
The Night of Broken Blades: woodcutters who tried to fell the sacred grove came back as undead with broken weapons and killed dozens overnight. That's why the monastery is shunned. (T.)
They say a jorogumo rules Shenmen now, out of Sze. Northridge folk shrug; Southbank folk spit. (T as rumor — none has come to Willowshore, far as anyone knows.)
Chou Mingxia of Sze died and came back as a ghost to rule. (T as rumor reaching town; treated as a scary far-off tale.)
This was a worse winter than anyone living remembers, and the next one has folk genuinely frightened the town can't feed itself. (T.)
A grateful local quietly tells you which shopkeeper to win over to get cold iron, fulus, peachwood, or ghost-touch gear for the season ahead. (T: a real lead, GM picks the contact.)
Zataku the fisher can smell the weather coming a day off — worth a visit before any trip on the water. (T.)
Hua De-ge at the Happy Kappa bathhouse knows every secret in town, and a good soak loosens their tongue. (T.)
A fresh, specific omen tied to the current scene — invent it from the haunt table or the threads in play; could be true or false. (?)
